page: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-48-lssd is an arm64-based server instance powered by the ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor. It features 48 dedicated physical cores running at 3.0 GHz with one thread per core, backed by 192 GB of RAM, which translates to a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. The instance includes 4020 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, providing high-speed local data access without requiring external block storage attachments.

In benchmark evaluations, this instance demonstrates strong multi-core performance, achieving a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 87014.41 and a Passmark CPU physics score of 13183.99. Memory performance is a notable strength, with a top-tier Passmark memory score and high read-only memory bandwidth reaching 5935.14 GB/sec for small cached blocks and 286.75 GB/sec for large uncached blocks. Database and web serving capabilities are also highly rated, as evidenced by a Passmark database operations score of 48182.95 and static web serving throughput of 97.21 GB/sec.

The ARM Neoverse-V2 architecture delivers high resource density and power efficiency, making it a cost-effective choice for scale-out workloads compared to traditional x86 architectures. However, the lack of x86-specific instruction sets like AVX-512 or AMX may limit its suitability for legacy software or specialized deep learning workloads that rely on those vector extensions. Given its balanced CPU-to-memory ratio, high-speed local NVMe storage, and strong database performance, this instance is well-suited for high-throughput web serving, Redis caching, relational databases, and multi-threaded data processing tasks.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4a-standard-48-lssd is an arm64 server instance powered by a 48-core ARMv8 Neoverse-V2 processor running at 3.0 GHz. It features 192 GB of RAM and 4020 GB of local NVMe SSD storage, offering a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. Benchmark results highlight strong multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 87014.41 and top-tier performance in database operations and static web serving. The architecture provides high memory bandwidth, reaching 286.75 GB/sec for large uncached blocks, and strong Redis performance at 98.12 million operations per second. While the ARM-based design lacks x86 vector extensions like AVX-512, it offers excellent resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for modern scale-out workloads. This instance is highly suited for database hosting, high-throughput web serving, caching layers, and multi-threaded data processing.
